guide: Open Start and type your business name, the service warning miles and days, your workshop days limit, the daily rate of each class and the date of the next tyre season change in the yellow cells.
Fill the Vehicle Register with one row per vehicle: class, purchase, odometer, last service, service interval and insurance. Miles are the demo unit, set your own.
Record every workshop visit in the Service Log and every repair in the Repair Log; the Service Due List shows miles and days to the next service by itself.
Add rental bookings of the next 14 days to Bookings Next 14 Days so the list can flag an overdue car that is booked this week (utilisation means rented days as a share of available days).
Add candidate dates in Workshop Slots; each one shows the booked days it loses and the best slot is marked.
Keep Renewals up to date: registration, insurance and inspection, with due date, cost and the date renewed.
Read Renewal Cost by Month for the next 12 months and set aside the amount the Renewal Cash Plan names.
Check Cost per 1,000 Miles, Repair Cost by Vehicle and Rental Days Lost every month to find the vehicle that costs most.
Record tyre sets in Tyre Dates and run the Tyre Planner before the season change.
Log bought and sold vehicles in Fleet Changes and use the Vehicle Register Check to fill the gaps.
Use the 18 calculators, print 12 sheets and 12 documents, follow 12 checklists and tap a message link to send a text with the details already written in.
Read the Fleet and Service Dashboard and the Charts every week. A one-car host uses the same sheets with one vehicle as a car-care and renewals diary.
To replace the demo data, clear the yellow cells of each sheet and type your own; no macros, works in Excel and Google Sheets, flat price with no per-vehicle fee, your data stays with you.

listing.title: Car Rental Fleet Register, Service and Renewals Excel Template: Service Due, Workshop Slots, Renewals Calendar, Cost per 1,000 Miles
listing.headline: Know which car needs service, which renewal is due and what each vehicle costs
listing.description:
Keep the cars of a small car or van rental business on the road in one Excel workbook. Built for an owner-operator and a manager who need to know which vehicle is due for service, which registration, insurance or inspection falls due next, and what each vehicle costs to keep.

The Vehicle Register holds one row per vehicle with class, purchase or financing, odometer, last service and insurance; miles since service, miles to the next service and the next service date fill in. The Service Due List flags every car by miles or months, whichever comes first, and marks a car that is past its interval and booked this week. Workshop Slots scores candidate dates by the booked days each one loses, so you book the slot that costs the fewest rentals. Renewals and Renewals by Vehicle show registration, insurance and inspection dates with overdue, 30-day and 60-day colours, and Renewal Cost by Month shows the next 12 months of cost for cash planning.

Cost per 1,000 Miles ranks vehicles against their class average with a rising-cost flag; Rental Days Lost turns workshop days into booked days and revenue lost; Tyre Dates, Inspection Log, Repair Log, Fleet Changes and Workshop Vendors round out the sheets. 18 calculators cover the service planner, the overdue-while-booked list, the slot planner, the renewals dashboard, the renewal cash plan, repair trend, tyre planner, cost ranking, register check, insurance compare, inspection planner, breakdown cost, interval check, vendor scorecard, backlog burn-down, 12-week forecast and downtime cost. Print 12 sheets and 12 documents, follow 12 checklists and send 34 ready text messages to the mechanic, tyre supplier, body repair shop, towing service, broker, lender, owner, manager, driver, detailer, bookkeeper, accountant and renters.

This is part five of the Car Rental Business suite. A standard .xlsx workbook with no macros and no subscription, with a demo copy full of sample data to explore first. Renters appear by first name only. Distances are in miles, the demo unit, set your own; amounts are plain numbers. It helps you keep track and does not promise results. Check your local rules for registration, inspection and insurance terms.

signature.name: Renewals dashboard
signature.why: registration, insurance and inspection dates across the fleet in one sorted list with overdue, 30-day and 60-day colours

signature.name: Renewal cash plan
signature.why: the cost of renewals over the next 12 months turned into the amount to set aside each month, so a big month never surprises you

signature.name: Repair cost trend
signature.why: repair and tyre cost per month and per 1,000 miles against the vehicle's own last 12 months, with a rising or steady flag

signature.name: Cost per 1,000 miles ranking
signature.why: vehicles ranked by maintenance cost per 1,000 miles against their class average so the money-eater is named

signature.name: Rental days lost to service
signature.why: workshop days turned into booked days and revenue lost at the class average daily rate

signature.name: Downtime cost
signature.why: workshop days times utilisation and daily rate compared with the repair bill itself

signature.name: Next-service forecast
signature.why: services due each week for 12 weeks in Base, Best and Worst cases, so you book the workshop ahead of the peak

competitors.lacks: charges per vehicle or per booking and keeps service and renewals in a module you cannot test, with no workshop slot that counts the booked days it loses
shows the dates but knows nothing of service intervals in miles, overdue cars with a booking this week or renewal colours
adds up costs but gives no cost per 1,000 miles, no class average and no rising-cost flag
plans yearly cash but has no renewal calendar by vehicle and no monthly set-aside for registration, insurance and inspection
records visits but never warns that a booked car is past its interval or which workshop slot loses the fewest rentals

paragraphs: Handover note of {set:company}, dated {today}. Vehicle: {col:vehicles.vehicle}, plate {col:vehicles.plate}, class {col:vehicles.class}, model year {col:vehicles.year}.
Odometer at handover: {col:vehicles.odometer} miles. Last service on {col:vehicles.last_service_date} at {col:vehicles.last_service_odometer} miles. Purchased on {col:vehicles.purchase_date}.
Status and dates only: this note records the vehicle and the dates. Check your local rules for registration transfer, records and any cover end date.
Both parties sign to confirm the odometer and the date.
documents.note: Sample wording: adapt it to your own business and check your local rules.

steps.label: Add the vehicle to the Vehicle Register
Fill plate, class, odometer and service interval
Add registration, insurance and inspection dates
Tell your insurance broker
Add it to the rate card and the booking calendar
Book the first service at the interval
Check the register for gaps
Open the Service Due List
Pull overdue cars from bookings this week
Book workshop slots in the Workshop Slots sheet
Tell the mechanic and the driver
Check the Workshop Calendar for busy days
Update the register after each visit
Add candidate dates for the vehicle
Pick the slot that loses the fewest booked days
Confirm the slot with the workshop
Move or swap any booking in the way
Plan the drop-off and the pick-up
Drop the vehicle off
Collect it and update the log
Check the invoice against the estimate
Record the visit in the Service Log
Update odometer and last service date
Ask for a clean and a check by the detailer
Put the vehicle back on the booking calendar
Open the Renewals Dashboard
Check overdue and due within 30 days
Check the Renewal Cash Plan against your set-aside
Ask the broker for quotes on insurance renewals
Send the cost to the bookkeeper
Check the renewal date and the cost
Check your local rules for what you need
Pay the renewal
Record the date renewed on the Renewals sheet
Keep the new registration with the vehicle file
Ask the broker for a quote
Compare with last year in Insurance Renewal Compare
Check your insurance terms and cover options
Choose and pay the renewal
Record the date renewed and the cost
Check the days the vehicle is free
Book the inspection slot
Move any booking in the way
Take the vehicle to the inspection
Record the result and the cost
Run the Tyre Planner for sets due
Order the sets
Book the fitting days
Plan the cars off the road, a few each day
Fit the tyres
Update the Tyre Dates sheet
Make sure the renter is safe
Call the towing service
Send a replacement car if one is free
Record the job in the Repair Log
Check the cost with the Breakdown Cost Check
Review repeat breakdowns of the vehicle
Check Replace or Sell figures in the finance part
Ask your lender for a payoff figure
Remove the vehicle from future bookings
Hand over the vehicle with status and dates only
Tell the broker to remove it
Mark it Sold on the register
Check tyres, lights and fluids each month
Service at the interval in miles or months
Renew registration and insurance on time
Book the inspection when due
Note every cost in the Service Log
